text:
Marathon Petroleum fell today as crude oil prices dropped for a second consecutive day on hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict. The company just reported quarterly earnings this morning, but broader energy market sentiment shifted as geopolitical risk eased—crude fell from recent highs, which directly pressures refiner profits since they buy oil as their raw material and sell refined products like gasoline and diesel.

The stock has lost nearly 10% over two weeks despite refineries running at a healthy 92.8% capacity, suggesting the recent leadership change announced on October 29th may have added uncertainty on top of the oil price weakness. When crude prices fall sharply and unexpectedly, even profitable refiners can see their stock punished as investors recalibrate near-term earnings expectations.
